Class CausalProcessedStream<K,V>

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalProcessedStream<K,V>
Type Parameters:
K - the forwarded key type
V - the forwarded value type
public final class CausalProcessedStream<K,V> extends Object
A causal stage bound to its processor, ready to declare sink(s) with to(String) and then terminate the topology with build(). Returned by CausalStream.process(ProcessorSupplier).

build() lives here, not on CausalStreamsBuilder, so that a causal topology is exactly one stream(...).process(...).to(...) chain: there is no term to open a second stage (see CausalStreamsBuilder's "one stage per topology" note).

      public CausalProcessedStream<K,V> to(String topic)
      Declares a sink topic for this stage, deferring its key/value serdes to the runtime's default serdes (default.key.serde/default.value.serde). The sink's topology node name defaults to topic — use to(String, String) to name it explicitly, required when the stage forwards to more than one sink and the delegate targets one by name.
      Parameters:
      topic - the sink topic name
      Returns:
      this, for declaring further sinks or withPartitioner(StreamPartitioner)

    • withPartitioner

      public CausalProcessedStream<K,V> withPartitioner(org.apache.kafka.streams.processor.StreamPartitioner<? super K, ? super V> partitioner)
      Sets the StreamPartitioner applied to every sink this stage declares (default: Kafka's own key-hash partitioner) — never configurable per-sink, so two sinks in the same stage can never drift onto different partitioners. partitioner must compute the partition from the key alone (never the value): the key is the only field causally related records share across topics, so a coarser-than-key shard function of the key is the intended use. Protocol null messages never reach this partitioner — CausalTopology wraps it in a decorator that routes each null message to the forwarding task's own partition.
      Parameters:
      partitioner - the partitioner to apply uniformly to every sink; must read only the key
      Returns:
      this

    • build

      public CausalTopology build()
      Freezes this stage and builds the single-stage CausalTopology, ready to be assembled into a real Kafka Streams Topology once a CausalStreams runtime supplies its props. Once built the stage is immutable: this handle can no longer add sinks or change the partitioner.
      Returns:
      the assembled single-stage CausalTopology
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if this stage has no source or no sink
